status: DRAFT for owner review (2026-09-26). Evidence map and decision structure only: nothing here is a performance prediction, a validation claim or a selection.
lane: FTREE (lane 26): architecture-specific failure trees, track 2 (architecture comparison preparation)
scope: Ways each candidate thrust architecture (hall_only, rf_hall, ecr_hall) could fail the programme against the RFP hard gates (CLAUDE.md RFP envelope: 180-230 km, 12-25 mN, < 1.5 kW, < 40 kg, 26,000 h mission, > 15,000 h firing, air + Xe). The rf_hall and ecr_hall arms change only the pre-ionization method; the downstream Hall accelerator, feed state, cathode and bus boundary are common, so nodes on the common elements carry all three architecture ids. Built to work without absolute Hall predictions: no node uses a Hall transport closure, screening candidate or withdrawn 0-D Hall result as a performance source. Analysis routes that would need absolute Hall performance are flagged (analysis_requires_admitted_hall_closure) and the one action that needs an admitted closure (A-HALLMAP) is blocked while the credible set is empty. Hall-closure uncertainty is confined to the ionization/discharge -> acceleration/thrust block; upstream nodes (gas supply) are marked upstream_hall_independent.
no_winner_statement: This file declares no winner and eliminates no architecture. Every node is decision_state 'open'. Evidence status describes whether published evidence makes a failure path credible; it is not a verdict on any Vyovrinda design. The ranking orders evidence to acquire, not architectures.

architectures.description: Single-stage Hall thruster: ionization and acceleration of the delivered atmospheric (and Xe) feed in one channel, plus the common cathode.
RF (inductive or helicon) pre-ionization stage feeding the common Hall accelerator. Whether the RF stage is magnetized (helicon) is a design choice; nodes that depend on it carry a 'condition'.
ECR (microwave or other resonant, magnetized) pre-ionization stage feeding the common Hall accelerator. Frequency and magnet type are design choices; no Vyovrinda value is assumed here.

failure_classes.name: ignition
failure_classes.description: The discharge (or pre-ionizer) does not start on the delivered feed without an allowed aid.

failure_classes.name: sustainment_extinction
failure_classes.description: The discharge extinguishes, oscillates destructively or leaves its operating window over the delivered feed envelope.

failure_classes.name: utilization
failure_classes.description: Too little of the atmospheric feed is ionized and accelerated to meet thrust within bus power; for two-stage arms, the pre-ionizer does not pay for itself.

failure_classes.name: cathode_limit
failure_classes.description: Cathode current, flow (Xe inventory), poisoning or life limits the programme.

failure_classes.name: thermal_limit
failure_classes.description: A component exceeds its temperature limit (Hall magnets and walls; RF coil/coupler; ECR magnets/resonator).

failure_classes.name: erosion_wall_life
failure_classes.description: Erosion, oxidation or coating of plasma-facing parts limits firing life.

failure_classes.name: power_limit
failure_classes.description: The bus-power gate cannot be met at the thrust gate.

failure_classes.name: mass_limit
failure_classes.description: The mass gate cannot be met (hardware plus Xe inventory).

failure_classes.name: control_startup
failure_classes.description: Start, restart or the Xe -> mixed -> atmosphere transition cannot be controlled.

failure_classes.name: interstage_loss
failure_classes.description: Ions made in the pre-ionizer are lost before the Hall acceleration zone, or the stages couple unstably.

failure_classes.name: rf_source_specific
failure_classes.description: RF-source-specific modes: E-H (capacitive-inductive) transition and hysteresis, impedance matching, magnetized-source field interaction, RF interference.

failure_classes.name: ecr_source_specific
failure_classes.description: ECR-specific modes: cutoff/overdense limit, interaction between ECR and Hall magnetic fields, microwave power chain.

evidence_status_rule.meaning: evidence_status says whether open-literature evidence makes the failure mechanism credible (physically operative in a relevant device or regime). It is not a gate verdict for a Vyovrinda design; that is decision_state, which is 'open' for every node in v1.

directions.supports: the source shows or states that the mechanism occurs (or limited a relevant device) in its domain
directions.contradicts: the source shows the mechanism did not occur, or was avoided, in a relevant device within its domain
directions.context: relevant but not decisive in either direction (different regime, design intent, mitigation validated only on another propellant, cause not attributed)

rule: supported: at least one 'supports' item and no 'contradicts' item
contradicted: at least one 'contradicts' item and no 'supports' item
unknown: no 'supports' and no 'contradicts' item (no evidence, or context only), or both present (conflicting)

unknown_basis.conflicting: both supporting and contradicting items exist; applicability decides and is not yet established
unknown_basis.no_evidence: no applicable open-literature item was found; evidence_gap says what is missing

elimination_rule.text: An architecture is eliminated only through explicit hard-gate logic: a node linked to a hard gate moves to resolved_fail for that architecture, and the supporting evidence is either (a) a measurement on Vyovrinda hardware or essentially identical hardware (EVIDENCE.md levels 1-2, quantity type measured) at the relevant operating condition, or (b) a physics bound that holds for every design of that architecture family independently of any Hall transport closure. Literature on other devices (level >= 3), screening candidates and unadmitted closures never eliminate. Proposed for the owner; not applied in v1 (eliminations = []).

actions.title: Thermal balance test
actions.description: Component temperatures (magnets, coils, RF coupler, ECR magnets/resonator, walls) at the air operating point in thermal-vacuum conditions.

action_effects.decides: The action's output alone settles the node, given only owner-fixed inputs (thresholds, margins, allocations, allowed Xe roles, operations-concept assumptions) and design-fixed inputs (component ratings and datasheet limits). If decision_quantity.requires_actions names another action, this action cannot decide the node.
action_effects.contributes: The action's output is a necessary member of the jointly sufficient set named in cheapest_resolution (or of another jointly sufficient set of the node's contributing actions); it is not sufficient alone.
action_effects.informs: The action narrows, prioritises or cross-checks the node but is not needed to settle it (for example a literature search, an unvalidated model, or a blocked Hall-map analysis).
action_effects.rule: decision_quantity.requires_actions lists every action whose output the threshold comparison needs. Each listed action is 'contributes' on the node (or is the single deciding action), no other action may 'decide' it, and every listed action is in cheapest_resolution.

nodes.title: Hall-stage cold start on atmospheric anode flow fails; start needs Xe
nodes.mechanism: Breakdown and transition to a self-sustained Hall discharge need enough neutral density and seed electrons in the channel; N2/O2 at ABEP-delivered density may not start without a noble-gas start.
nodes.physical_cause: Higher ionization and inelastic (vibrational, dissociation) energy cost of N2/O2 than Xe, and channel neutral density set by the intake rather than a flow controller.

evidence.statement: 'The PPS1350-TSD was always ignited with xenon. After ignition, a smooth transition from 100% xenon to 100% nitrogen or N2/O2 mixture at the anode was carried out; the cathode continued to work with xenon.'
evidence.applicability: Test procedure on a 1.4 kW-limited laboratory Hall thruster; air-only ignition was not reported as attempted.

evidence.statement: The integrated RAM-EP system 'was successfully ignited with the atmospheric propellant provided by the PFG (operating at 4.7 mg/s mass flow rate of pure N2-O2)'; the intake let the RAM-HET 'ignite a pure N2-O2 flow at an acceleration voltage equal to 300 V and an ionization voltage equal to 100 V'.
evidence.applicability: Double-stage Hall thruster in a ground facility with a Xe-fed cathode (cathode ignition with xenon, Sec. III.F); not a single-stage Hall and not flight density.

evidence.statement: 'HET ignitions and stable operation are achieved when the neutral gas density is sufficiently high'; estimated thruster-inlet neutral density 1e17-1e18 m^-3, 'from one to two orders of magnitude' below the ionization region of standard HETs.
evidence.applicability: Source's design estimate for its intake; the Vyovrinda delivered density is set by the upstream chain (A-FLOWENV).

evidence.statement: 'the RAM-HET also requires injection of Xe to aid the ignition of the thruster, as well as to operate the neutraliser' (citing the SITAEL RAM-EP papers).
evidence.applicability: Secondary statement about the SITAEL RAM-HET.

decision_quantity.quantity: Start success per attempt on atmospheric-only anode flow at the delivered feed state (IF-A5); Xe used per start when a Xe start is used
decision_quantity.threshold: Every start the operations concept needs succeeds without Xe, or with a Xe per start that fits the air_xe rules and the Xe allocation (see N-CTL-02) (TBD - requires the owner's restart count and Xe allocation)
decision_quantity.requires: restart count (A-OPS, from owner assumptions) and allowed Xe roles (air_xe gate TBD)
requires_owner_inputs: operations-concept assumptions for the restart count

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate Hall-stage start on the atmospheric feed state, or a Xe-assisted start whose Xe per start fits the Xe allocation.

nodes.title: RF pre-ionizer does not break down on N2/O2 at the delivered pressure
nodes.mechanism: Inductive/helicon breakdown on molecular gases at low pressure needs higher fields than on noble gases; the source may need a noble-gas start.
nodes.physical_cause: Higher ionization energy and electron energy losses of N2/O2 relative to Ar/Xe.

evidence.statement: RIT-10 EBB: 'The argon is used to ignite the thruster, as the ignition with N2/O2 was found to be much more difficult ... xenon ignites even better than argon.'
evidence.applicability: RF (inductive) ion thruster discharge chamber, Giessen facility; a gridded RF discharge, not an RF pre-ionizer feeding a Hall stage.

evidence.statement: A frequency 'equal or higher than 27.12 MHz' was chosen 'as it leads to easier ignition at low pressure' (from literature and preliminary numerics).
evidence.applicability: Design guidance for an inductive plasma thruster; not a measurement.

decision_quantity.quantity: RF-source breakdown on the atmospheric feed at the delivered pressure with the available RF power
decision_quantity.threshold: Breakdown without a noble-gas start, or noble-gas start within the air_xe rules (TBD - requires the owner's air_xe rules on Xe roles)
decision_quantity.requires: delivered pressure (A-FLOWENV) and allowed Xe roles

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate RF-source breakdown on the atmospheric feed at delivered pressure, or an allowed noble-gas start.

nodes.title: ECR pre-ionizer does not break down on air at the delivered pressure
nodes.mechanism: Microwave/ECR breakdown needs the resonance condition inside the source and enough neutral density for the electron energy gain to produce ionization.
nodes.physical_cause: Resonance field, wave coupling and electron energy losses on N2/O2.

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'experimental demonstration of plasma ignition in an electron-cyclotron-resonance atmosphere-breathing electric propulsion source at pressures representative of very low Earth orbit' and 'sustained plasma discharge at pressures consistent with conditions expected after intake compression at altitudes near 200 km'.
evidence.applicability: Laboratory ECR ABEP source with a MHz-range birdcage resonator. The abstract (re-read via Crossref 2026-09-26) does not state the gas, so air or N2/O2 breakdown is not established; not decisive until the full text (L-ECRHALL) gives the composition.

evidence.statement: Microwave cathode: 'Plasma formation was very reliable and never required the use of any separate ignition' (xenon and argon).
evidence.applicability: Noble gases only; nitrogen-oxygen not attempted (Sec. V).

decision_quantity.quantity: ECR-source breakdown on the atmospheric feed at the delivered pressure
decision_quantity.threshold: Breakdown without a noble-gas start, or noble-gas start within the air_xe rules (TBD - requires the owner's air_xe rules on Xe roles)
decision_quantity.requires: delivered pressure (A-FLOWENV) and allowed Xe roles

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate ECR-source breakdown on the atmospheric feed at delivered pressure.
nodes.evidence_gap: No open item read so far establishes ECR breakdown on air or N2/O2: S-STASTNY2026 reports ignition at VLEO-representative pressures but its abstract does not state the gas, and its CC BY full text is targeted by L-ECRHALL; S-DIAMANT2009 covers noble gases only.

nodes.title: Pre-ionizer seed plasma does not lower the Hall-stage start requirement
nodes.mechanism: The two-stage start benefit (seed plasma from the pre-ionizer triggering the Hall discharge at lower feed density) may not materialize if the seed does not reach the Hall channel.
nodes.physical_cause: Interstage loss of seed charge and field-line connection between the stages.

evidence.statement: Double-stage RAM-HET: 'the first stage showed a good capability to ionize the flow provided by the PFG'.
evidence.applicability: DC magnetic-confinement first stage, not RF or ECR; does not isolate the start threshold.

nodes.evidence_gap: No open source found that measures the Hall-stage start threshold with vs without an RF or ECR seed on atmospheric gases.

decision_quantity.quantity: Minimum feed density (or pressure) for Hall-stage start with the pre-ionizer on vs off
decision_quantity.threshold: Start at the lowest delivered feed state of the envelope with the pre-ionizer on (PROPOSED form; margin TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: delivered-feed envelope (A-FLOWENV)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate that the pre-ionizer lowers (or at least does not raise) the Hall-stage start requirement at the delivered feed state.

nodes.title: Hall stage extinguishes or runs unstably on N2/O2 within the needed window
nodes.mechanism: The sustained operating window (voltage, flow, magnetic field) on molecular propellant is narrow; outside it the discharge extinguishes or enters strongly oscillating modes.
nodes.physical_cause: Ionization balance of N2/O2 at channel density; mode changes with magnetic-field setting.

evidence.statement: P5 on N2: the text states the discharge cannot be sustained above 275 V or below 225 V; all five setpoints N1-N5 ran (repo audit finding F4 reads 275 V as an approximate boundary).
evidence.locator: Repo audit p5_n2_measurement_audit_findings_v1.json: admissible_targets.sustained_discharge, finding F4
evidence.applicability: 5-kW-class P5, 5.0-5.4 mg/s N2 anode, Xe cathode, facility pressure 1.1-2.1e-5 Torr.

evidence.statement: ECHT on N2: 3 of 7 thrust runs flagged strongly unstable; the thruster changed modes during calibration.
evidence.applicability: ECHT, 2.06 mg/s N2, 180-220 V, facility pressure 0.8-2.5e-4 Torr, argon cathode.

evidence.statement: PPS1350-TSD on 1.27N2+O2: 'Stable operation occurs with a mass flow rate as low as 2.1 mg/s' and 'The thruster has operated stably during the 10 hours test.'
evidence.applicability: Laboratory Hall thruster, Xe cathode, Xe start, 10-h firing.

evidence.statement: RAM-HET standalone: 'Attempts to operate the thruster with N2-O2 mixture were performed but a certain amount of xenon (~1.5 mg/s) has always been necessary to prevent the flame out'.
evidence.applicability: Double-stage RAM-HET in standalone configuration.

decision_quantity.quantity: Sustained operating window (V_d, mass flow, magnet setting) of the Hall stage on the delivered composition, with oscillation amplitude and extinction boundary
decision_quantity.threshold: Sustained at every design operating point on the delivered composition without continuous Xe, with an oscillation bound (PROPOSED; amplitude TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: delivered composition (A-FLOWENV); owner margin

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate sustained, bounded-oscillation Hall-stage operation on the delivered atmospheric composition without continuous Xe.

nodes.title: Delivered-flow range over altitude and solar activity exceeds the sustainment range
nodes.mechanism: The intake-delivered flow varies with altitude (180-230 km) and solar activity; if the ratio of maximum to minimum delivered flow is larger than the flow range over which the discharge is sustained, throttling fails at one end.
nodes.physical_cause: Atmospheric density variability transmitted through the intake/compressor chain to the thruster interface.

evidence.statement: 'In a RAM-EP system, the properties of the neutral flow inside the thruster channel critically depends on the intake configuration and on the atmospheric conditions outside of the system.'
evidence.applicability: General statement by an ABEP developer; the Vyovrinda envelope comes from A-FLOWENV.

decision_quantity.quantity: Ratio of maximum to minimum delivered mass flow at IF-A5 over 180-230 km and solar states, against the sustained flow range of the Hall stage (and pre-ionizer)
decision_quantity.threshold: Sustained flow range contains the delivered-flow envelope, or the flow control keeps the feed inside it (PROPOSED)
decision_quantity.requires: A-FLOWENV (upstream, Hall-independent) and M-SUSWIN

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show that the delivered-flow envelope lies inside the demonstrated sustained flow range, or that flow control keeps it there.

nodes.title: Two-stage coupling: excess acceleration-stage current or unstable interaction limits the Hall stage
nodes.mechanism: With a separate ionization stage, electron current into the acceleration stage and the interaction of the two discharges can cap the usable acceleration voltage or destabilize operation.
nodes.physical_cause: Electron supply and potential distribution between stages; power-supply coupling.

evidence.statement: 'the current circulating in the acceleration stage was always significantly higher than expected. This phenomenon posed a limit to the applicable acceleration voltage and, in turn, to the achievable thrust'; in standalone Xe tests both supplies went to current limitation and both voltages dropped to around 100 V.
evidence.locator: Sec. IV (pdf p. 10); Sec. III.E (pdf p. 7)
evidence.applicability: Double-stage Hall (DC first stage); mechanism class is two-stage coupling, not specific to RF or ECR.

decision_quantity.quantity: Acceleration-stage current and usable acceleration voltage with the pre-ionizer on, and stability of the coupled discharges
decision_quantity.threshold: Acceleration voltage and current at the design point reachable with bounded oscillation (PROPOSED)
decision_quantity.requires: owner-fixed thresholds and design-fixed inputs only

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate the design acceleration voltage and current with the pre-ionizer on, without runaway acceleration-stage current.

nodes.title: Low ion utilization of N2/O2 in the Hall stage prevents 12 mN within the bus power
nodes.mechanism: A small ionized fraction of the atmospheric feed (and beam divergence) gives low thrust per unit flow and per unit power.
nodes.physical_cause: Energy sinks of molecular gases (vibrational excitation, dissociation) and low channel neutral density at ABEP flows.

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'The helicon Hall thruster performance during operation with argon and nitrogen is characterized by low beam divergence efficiency and low propellant utilization efficiency.'
evidence.applicability: Helicon Hall thruster, nitrogen at 200 V.

evidence.statement: 'The computation of the ionisation efficiency shows that this last is lower for nitrogen than for xenon'; conclusion: 'a substantial deterioration of performance with respect to Xe, especially due to the low ionization efficiency of the atmospheric propellants'.
evidence.locator: Sec. II.B (pdf p. 3); Sec. IV (pdf p. 11)
evidence.applicability: PPS1350-TSD and RIT-10 in laboratory facilities.

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'Simplified collision frequency estimations indicate that N2 vibrational losses are likely the dominant electron energy loss channel across the tested ratios.'
evidence.applicability: Helicon plasma, N2:O2 1:4 to 4:1; an energy-sink mechanism, not a Hall-stage measurement.

decision_quantity.quantity: Ion (current) utilization and resulting thrust on the delivered composition at the discharge power left by the electrical closure
decision_quantity.threshold: >= 12 mN sustained on air within the 1.5 kW bus (RFP)
decision_quantity.requires: A-ELEC for the discharge power available

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate >= 12 mN on the delivered atmospheric composition within the discharge power the common bus boundary leaves.

nodes.title: RF pre-ionization gains less utilization than its power costs (thrust-to-power falls)
nodes.mechanism: The RF stage raises the ionized fraction only slightly while adding its full power (and generator loss) to the bus.
nodes.physical_cause: RF energy per delivered ion (source cost plus interstage loss) above the Hall stage's own ionization cost.

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'During two-stage operation, the thrust of the helicon Hall thruster marginally increased with radio frequency power, but the propulsive efficiency and thrust-to-power both decreased with increasing radio frequency power. Probe diagnostics suggest that gains were realized by a slight increase in propellant efficiency, but that the rate of increase was not sufficient to overcome the increase in power.'
evidence.applicability: Helicon Hall thruster; the abstract does not state the gas used in two-stage operation.

evidence.statement: Hall thrusters at low voltage 'suffer from poor propellant utilization efficiency, especially when using alternative propellants, but using an RF-augmented system may increase the propellant utilization efficiency' (citing the Shabshelowitz thesis).
evidence.applicability: Secondary statement of potential, no numbers.

decision_quantity.quantity: Thrust at fixed bus power with the RF stage on vs the hall_only arm at the same feed state
decision_quantity.threshold: rf_hall thrust at 1.5 kW bus >= 12 mN; break-even against the hall_only arm is PROPOSED as the architecture-benefit criterion
decision_quantity.requires: A-BREAKEVEN surfaces; common bus boundary (A-ELEC)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate that the RF stage raises thrust at fixed bus power, or meets 12 mN within 1.5 kW including its own power.

nodes.title: ECR pre-ionization gains less utilization on air than its power costs
nodes.mechanism: ECR heating raises ionization strongly on Xe, but on air a larger share of electron energy goes into dissociation and molecular excitation, so the gain per watt may not pay for the microwave power.
nodes.physical_cause: Electron energy losses of N2/O2 and the microwave power chain efficiency.

evidence.statement: 'the ECR-indicative behaviour seen with xenon is not demonstrated for air, with figure 6(a) showing a general suppression of extracted current from an initial 0.06 A to 0.01 A at increased |B| values'; abstract: the Xe extracted current rises 3.9 times up to about 150 mT at the antenna, 'whereas an applied field does not increase the extracted current with air at nominal conditions' (a non-zero field helps with air at reduced neutral densities).
evidence.applicability: 2.45 GHz microwave plasma cathode (electron source), 24-70 W; not an ion pre-ionizer for a Hall stage.

evidence.statement: Abstract: an ECR-stage 2-stage cylindrical Hall thruster design with 'preliminary data showing favorable comparison to existing cylindrical Hall thrusters'.
evidence.applicability: Abstract only; gas, utilization and power trade not stated in the abstract, so it does not bear on the air-specific gain per watt.

decision_quantity.quantity: Thrust at fixed bus power with the ECR stage on vs the hall_only arm at the same feed state
decision_quantity.threshold: ecr_hall thrust at 1.5 kW bus >= 12 mN; break-even against the hall_only arm is PROPOSED as the architecture-benefit criterion
decision_quantity.requires: A-BREAKEVEN surfaces; common bus boundary (A-ELEC)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate that the ECR stage raises thrust at fixed bus power on air, or meets 12 mN within 1.5 kW including its own power.

nodes.title: Ions made in the RF stage are lost before the Hall acceleration zone
nodes.mechanism: Wall recombination, radial diffusion and field-line geometry between the RF source and the Hall channel remove ions and electrons before they reach the acceleration zone.
nodes.physical_cause: Interstage geometry and magnetic connection; molecular-ion recombination at walls.

evidence.statement: Two-stage gains came from 'a slight increase in propellant efficiency' (abstract).
evidence.applicability: Consistent with interstage loss but does not isolate transmission.

nodes.evidence_gap: No open measurement of RF-to-Hall interstage ion transmission on atmospheric gases was found.

decision_quantity.quantity: Interstage ion transmission fraction (ion current entering the acceleration zone / ion current produced in the RF stage)
decision_quantity.threshold: >= the transmission the break-even surfaces require at the design point (TBD - requires the break-even surfaces evaluated at a Vyovrinda design point)
decision_quantity.requires: A-BREAKEVEN for the required transmission; the transmission itself is the measured quantity (interstage ion flux in the common-condition test). The interstage model output is unvalidated and only informs.

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show RF-to-Hall interstage transmission at or above the break-even requirement.

nodes.title: Ions made in the ECR stage are trapped or lost before the Hall acceleration zone
nodes.mechanism: Strong fields needed for resonance confine the plasma near the production zone and near magnet surfaces, raising wall loss and hindering transport to the next stage.
nodes.physical_cause: Resonance field magnitude (0.0875 T at 2.45 GHz, derived) and magnet-surface proximity of the resonance zone.

evidence.statement: Higher frequencies need higher fields; 'These high magnetic fields make it difficult for plasma to diffuse away from ECR plasma production zones. Additionally, ECR zones occur much closer to the magnet surface which gives rise to increases in plasma losses to the walls.'
evidence.locator: Section 'Basic Design and Discharge Performance Implications' (pdf p. 8)
evidence.applicability: ECR ion-thruster discharge (xenon); the same transport physics applies to an ECR pre-ionizer feeding a downstream stage.

evidence.statement: An ECR ionization stage feeding a cylindrical Hall stage was designed and preliminarily tested (abstract).
evidence.applicability: Abstract only.

decision_quantity.quantity: Interstage ion transmission fraction from the ECR zone to the acceleration zone
decision_quantity.threshold: >= the transmission the break-even surfaces require at the design point (TBD - requires the break-even surfaces evaluated at a Vyovrinda design point)
decision_quantity.requires: A-BREAKEVEN for the required transmission; the transmission itself is the measured quantity (interstage ion flux in the common-condition test). The interstage model output is unvalidated and only informs.

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show ECR-to-Hall interstage transmission at or above the break-even requirement.

nodes.title: E-H (or helicon) mode transition with hysteresis drops the RF stage to a low-density mode
nodes.mechanism: Inductive sources have a weak capacitive E mode and a dense inductive H mode; the E->H transition occurs at a higher coil current than H->E, so a power, flow or composition change can drop the source to E mode and recovery needs more power.
nodes.physical_cause: Nonlinear electron power balance (hysteresis); composition-dependent transition power in N2/O2.

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'The E-to-H transition occurs at a larger coil current than the H-to-E transition, and a range of currents between these values supports either E or H mode. This effect is called hysteresis', attributed to nonlinear effects in the electron power balance.
evidence.applicability: General inductive-discharge physics (processing plasmas).

evidence.statement: Abstract: with N2:O2 from 1:4 to 4:1, 'mode transition power exhibits notable reduction at N2:O2 = 1:4'; N2:O2 of about 2:3 is a transition region between O2- and N2-dominated behaviour.
evidence.applicability: Helicon plasma for air-breathing thrusters; transition power depends on composition.

evidence.statement: Abstract: plasma morphology, emission spectrum and spatial profile 'change significantly during mode transitions with the N2-Ar ratio'.
evidence.applicability: N2-Ar helicon plasma at fixed power and field.

decision_quantity.quantity: RF power / coil current margin above the H->E (or helicon mode) transition over the delivered composition and flow envelope
decision_quantity.threshold: Operating point above the down-transition everywhere in the envelope with a margin (PROPOSED; margin TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: composition envelope (A-FLOWENV)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate RF-stage operation above its mode down-transition over the delivered composition envelope with margin.

nodes.title: Impedance mismatch (reflected power) across ignition, Xe <-> air change and flow envelope
nodes.mechanism: Plasma ignition and gas/flow changes shift the load impedance; a fixed match reflects power, an automatic match must track it.
nodes.physical_cause: Plasma-dependent antenna load (resistance and reactance).

evidence.statement: 'Once the plasma is ignited, a frequency shift and a corresponding impedance change will happen. This requires tuning to shift back to the original resonance condition.'
evidence.applicability: Resonant birdcage-antenna IPT design (citing prior observations).

evidence.statement: 400 W at 13.56 MHz coupled 'via a customized pi-type matching network to maintain system impedance matched across all operational conditions. Reflected power is kept below 2%, for all the tests.'
evidence.applicability: Helicon thruster on air 4.5-27 sccm and on krypton, laboratory matching network.

decision_quantity.quantity: Reflected power fraction over ignition, Xe <-> air transition and the flow envelope with the chosen matching approach
decision_quantity.threshold: Reflected power within the RF generator rating and inside the bus ledger (PROPOSED; value TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: bus-ledger margin for reflected power (A-ELEC); RF generator rating (design input)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate matched RF operation (bounded reflected power) through ignition and the Xe -> air transition.

nodes.title: Magnetized RF (helicon) source field interacts with the Hall magnetic circuit
nodes.condition: Applies only if a magnetized (helicon) RF source is chosen.
nodes.mechanism: The helicon solenoid field superposes on the Hall circuit field, distorting the Hall B(z) topology or the helicon-region field.
nodes.physical_cause: Field magnitudes of the same order in adjacent regions.

evidence.statement: Helicon thrusters use an external solenoid field 'typically in the range between 100 and 1000 G'; 600 G at the magnetic throat in the air test.
evidence.locator: Sec. I (pdf p. 1); Sec. II (pdf p. 2)
evidence.applicability: Standalone helicon thruster.

evidence.statement: Hall-thruster centreline field 'is typically below 1 kG'.
evidence.applicability: General statement on Hall thrusters.

nodes.evidence_gap: No open source quantifies the helicon-Hall field interaction on atmospheric gases (S-SHABSHELOWITZ2014 full text may; not accessible).

decision_quantity.quantity: Deviation of the Hall-channel B(z) and of the helicon-region field under superposition, over the magnet-current schedule
decision_quantity.threshold: Hall B(z) within the Vyovrinda design tolerance (TBD, docs/hallmap/)
decision_quantity.requires: owner-fixed thresholds and design-fixed inputs only

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show by field analysis that the helicon field leaves the Hall B(z) within design tolerance (if a magnetized RF source is chosen).

nodes.title: RF interference coupling into the Hall discharge circuit, cathode or PPU sensing
nodes.mechanism: RF fields and currents couple into the discharge supply, cathode keeper and control sensing, disturbing regulation or protection.
nodes.physical_cause: Near-field coupling from the RF antenna and return paths.
nodes.evidence_gap: No open-literature source on RF-to-Hall electromagnetic interference was found in this lane's search; S-RABUNAL2024 uses RF-compensated probes (diagnostic practice), which is not evidence on thruster electronics.

decision_quantity.quantity: Disturbance on discharge current/voltage regulation and keeper/cathode supply with RF on
decision_quantity.threshold: No loss of regulation or protection trips (PROPOSED)
decision_quantity.requires: owner-fixed thresholds and design-fixed inputs only

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate regulated Hall and cathode supplies with the RF stage on.

nodes.title: Cutoff (overdense) limit: ECR-stage density saturates below the Hall-stage feed need
nodes.mechanism: Microwaves launched from the low-field side are reflected where the plasma frequency exceeds the wave frequency (O-mode cutoff n_c(f); the X-mode R-cutoff lies at lower density), capping density unless another wave mode or launch is used.
nodes.physical_cause: n_c(f) = epsilon_0 m_e (2 pi f)^2 / e^2 (derived values D-ECR-NC-*).

evidence.statement: At 2.45 GHz and 750 W the measured near-grid density 'was as high as 6x10^10 #/cm3, very close to the cutoff density at this frequency'; the second-generation engine moved to 5.85 GHz; above cutoff 'the microwaves are no longer absorbed, but reflected to regions of lower field strength'. The same report attributes a later density saturation near the ion grid more likely to high utilization than to cutoff ('The high calculated grid currents suggest that the latter possibility likely prevails').
evidence.locator: Sections 'Basic Design and Discharge Performance Implications' (pdf p. 8) and 'Early Microwave Ion Source Development' (pdf p. 11); section 'Plasma density' of the discharge results (pdf p. 21)
evidence.applicability: HiPEP ECR ion-thruster discharge on xenon.

evidence.statement: Estimated cavity plasma densities 1e18-1e19 m^-3 (xenon) and 6e17-3e18 m^-3 (argon) exceed the stated 'critical density at 5.8 GHz = 4x10^17 m^-3'.
evidence.applicability: Microwave cathode; densities inferred from an ion-migration current limit, not measured.

evidence.statement: Cut-off density at 2.45 GHz is 7.4e16 m^-3; 'the electron density observed in microwave cathodes is significantly higher than nc', so microwaves do not penetrate the overdense bulk and heating occurs near the antenna.
evidence.applicability: Microwave cathodes operate overdense; applicability to an ion-producing pre-ionizer not shown.

decision_quantity.quantity: Required ECR-stage density (or ion flux) against n_c(f) for the chosen frequency and launch
decision_quantity.threshold: n_e <= n_c(f), the O-mode cutoff, for low-field-side launch (a low-field-side X-mode wave meets the R-cutoff, omega_pe^2 = omega (omega - omega_ce), at a lower density still); above n_c only with a demonstrated overdense heating route (physics bound)
decision_quantity.requires: required ion flux from A-INTERSTAGE

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show the ECR stage reaches the ion flux the Hall stage needs, below cutoff or by a demonstrated overdense route.

nodes.title: ECR resonance field interacts with the Hall magnetic circuit
nodes.mechanism: The resonance surface needs |B| = 2 pi f m_e / e near the source while the Hall channel needs its own B(z); the ECR magnets distort the Hall topology and the Hall circuit (and its current schedule between Xe and air setpoints) moves the resonance surface.
nodes.physical_cause: Resonance field (0.0875 T at 2.45 GHz, derived) is several times the peak radial field of a Hall channel such as P5 (130-162.5 G).

evidence.statement: 'For f = 2.45 GHz, the corresponding ECR magnetic-field strength BECR is 87.5 mT.'
evidence.applicability: Physics statement; reproduced by D-ECR-B-2.45GHZ.

evidence.statement: P5 peak radial B 162.5 G at the Xe setpoints and 130 G at the N2 setpoints; coils tuned at N3 and held.
evidence.locator: hallthruster_bridge/cases/p5_xenon.json source field (Table 4); p5_n2_measurement_audit_findings_v1.json finding F6
evidence.applicability: A 5-kW-class Hall thruster; illustrative magnitude, not a Vyovrinda design value.

evidence.statement: Hall centreline field 'is typically below 1 kG'.
evidence.applicability: General statement.

evidence.statement: Abstract: a 'MHz-range birdcage resonator in combination with a tailored magnetic field' sustained an ECR discharge at VLEO-representative pressure.
evidence.applicability: A lower resonance frequency lowers the required field; route relevant to the interaction, not a demonstration with a Hall circuit.

nodes.evidence_gap: No open measurement of an ECR stage operating with an adjacent Hall circuit on atmospheric gases (S-DIAMANT2010 full text may contain one; closed).

decision_quantity.quantity: Resonance-surface location and Hall B(z) deviation under superposed fields over the magnet-current schedule
decision_quantity.threshold: Resonance surface inside the ECR region and Hall B(z) within design tolerance at every scheduled setpoint (TBD, docs/hallmap/)
decision_quantity.requires: owner-fixed thresholds and design-fixed inputs only

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show by field analysis (then test) that the ECR resonance and the Hall B(z) coexist at every scheduled setpoint.

nodes.title: Microwave power chain (generator, transmission, coupler) efficiency or life insufficient
nodes.mechanism: DC-to-microwave conversion and transmission losses add to the bus and to waste heat; the generator must survive the firing and mission hours.
nodes.physical_cause: Generator technology efficiency and wear-out.

nodes.title: Emitter poisoning by oxygen from the feed, plume backflow or ram exposure
nodes.mechanism: Oxygen on the thermionic emitter raises the work function, cutting emission and destabilizing the cathode (plume mode), with erosion at high temperature.
nodes.physical_cause: Surface chemistry of BaO-W and LaB6 emitters in oxidizing environments.

evidence.statement: 'exposure of the emitter materials, such as barium-oxide impregnated tungsten (BaO-W) or lanthanum-hexaboride (LaB6), to oxygen results in poisoning of the material surface and prompts a significant decrease in the current density at even minimal values of air pressure'; operation of a LaB6 hollow cathode on xenon containing a 12% fraction of a 0.48O2 + 0.52N2 mixture 'results in significant erosion of the emitter and cathode structure' (citing refs [9, 10] and [1] = S-ANDREUSSI2022).
evidence.applicability: Secondary statements; primary sources not read (S-ANDREUSSI2022 targeted by L-CATHODE).

evidence.statement: Abstract: on an unused segmented LaB6 emitter the plume-mode region expanded during a discharge experiment; the surface showed 'oxygen and carbon detection', but 'the dominant substance in the region where carbon is detected was lanthanum carbide', where 'an increase in the work function is indicated', which 'appears to increase the plasma instability'; plume mode 'severely degrades the overall cathode lifetime'.
evidence.applicability: Laboratory LaB6 hollow cathode; the work-function rise is attributed mainly to carbon (lanthanum carbide), oxygen is only detected, and the contamination source is not an air feed. Weak for oxygen poisoning, so context only.

evidence.statement: ECHT tests ran a degraded BaO emitter cathode (IonTech HCN-252) on argon.
evidence.applicability: Degradation cause not attributed.

evidence.statement: After two days of RAM-HET Xe / N2-O2 testing 'cathode ignition could not be achieved anymore'; inspection showed 'a damaged emitter'.
evidence.applicability: Cause not attributed by the source.

evidence.statement: 'Use of a thermionic hollow cathode, perhaps with a relatively oxygen-tolerant LaB6 insert, coupled with a small on-board supply of xenon may be an adequate solution'; for long missions the author assumes hot parts exposed to the oxidizing environment should be avoided.
evidence.applicability: Design judgement citing S-GOEBEL2007.

evidence.statement: With N2 or N2/O2 at the anode, 'the cathode continued to work with xenon'.

ranking_rule.text: For each architecture, rank every eligible action by how many of that architecture's open nodes it decides, then by how many distinct hard gates those decided nodes link, then by how many nodes it contributes to (needed jointly with other actions), then by how many it informs, then cheapest kind first, then action id. Ties are broken only by these keys. Actions touching no node of the architecture are omitted.
ranking_rule.eligibility: An action is eligible if blocked_by is empty. Blocked actions (today only A-HALLMAP, blocked by the empty credible set and incomplete O4 dispositions) are listed separately with the nodes they touch and are not ranked.
ranking_rule.no_weighting: No weights, probabilities or expert scores enter the ranking. The only non-count key is the categorical cost rank literature < analysis < measurement, used as a tie-break after all counts.
